Note::NlpAccessor::mask_emails¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::mask_emails() const

Hide Mailboxes Without Hiding Nearby Handles¶

mask_emails() replaces each ASCII email-shaped span with [EMAIL]. It is narrower than mask_pii: URLs, social handles, numbers, and dates remain available for separate policy decisions.

The local part accepts ASCII letters, digits, ., _, %, +, and -. The domain accepts ASCII letters, digits, dots, and hyphens and must end in a letter-only suffix of at least two characters. Matching is case-sensitive only in preservation terms: the entire matched address is removed, so letter case does not affect the placeholder.

a+b@example.co.uk and subdomains are recognized. a@b, @handle, and non-ASCII mailbox syntax are not. The boundary before an address prevents a substring inside a larger email-like token from being masked accidentally. Sentence punctuation after a valid address remains outside the replacement.

The method is shape-preserving, non-mutating, and Text-only. It allocates one fresh packed Text result. Cells without @ bypass recognition immediately. Undefined input propagates; empty shapes remain defined and empty. Existing [EMAIL] placeholders are idempotent.

Example 1: Plus Addressing And Subdomains¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"a+b@example.co.uk", "x.y@sub.example.io"})
        .nlp().mask_emails()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["[EMAIL]", "[EMAIL]"]

Example 2: Punctuation, Incomplete Addresses, And Mentions¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"mail x@y.io, keep a@b and @handle"})
        .nlp().mask_emails()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["mail [EMAIL], keep a@b and @handle"]

The comma survives, while incomplete mail syntax and the social handle remain.

Example 3: Empty, Undefined, And Bytes¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::string>{})
                       .nlp().mask_emails();
std::cout << "emails empty dim=" << empty.dim()
          << " numel=" << empty.numel() << '\n';
std::cout << "emails undefined=" << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().mask_emails().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes(
      std::vector<std::string>{"a@b.io"}, std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{1})
      .nlp().mask_emails();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "emails Bytes: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

emails empty dim=1 numel=0
emails undefined=false
emails Bytes: rejected

See Also¶

  • mask_mentions: mask standalone @ handles without treating emails as handles.

  • mask_pii: combine email masking with other categories.
